full_judgment:
"The present appeal is directed against the decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge at the re-hearing under the second order of remand by this court. The learned Subordinate Judge has again taken the view that the plaintiffs had hopelessly failed to establish any immemorial user of the right of may which would give one to a presumption of lost grant. although he found that in the C.S. records filially published in the year 1898, the disputed pathway had been recorded as such a pathway. But that was, according to the learned Subordinate Judge, not enough because upon the principle enunciated by his lordship Ibrahim, J: long enjoyment of right claimed from time immemorial meant enjoyment From beyond living, memory. Therefore, the evidence of the C.S. records could by no means be said to take it beyond the period of living memory." 

 It is apparent that the mentioning in the kabala of the existence of the disputed pathway sometime over 50 years back is a strong presumption that the user of the right is nothing but as of right that is to say it has a lawful origin and therefore it cannot be brushed aside by saying that walking ever other's land even for hundred years does not create any easement right."
